observed.workerResultLine: PALIMPSEST_WORK_RESULT {"kind":"HOST_FAILURE","detail":"refusing to run this worker: UNCLASSIFIED worker-visible capability(ies): working_directory - an unknown capability is not assumed safe, so the worker must not start"}

whyThisIsCorrectBehaviour: The capability gate is FAIL-CLOSED by design: an unclassified worker-visible capability refuses the worker rather than assuming it safe. The refusal is the mechanism working, not a defect in the assay.
rootCause: The installed first-party DSH is 0.2.1-rc.2 while the product's read-boundary contract was qualified against 0.2.0-rc.2. That release added the `working_directory` user-context capability, which is absent from host/deployment/runtime/capability_classes.js.
whyNotFixedHere: Classifying a new capability changes PRODUCTION security semantics (host/deployment/runtime/capability_classes.js), which E1RC explicitly forbids without a separate stop-and-report. Deciding whether `working_directory` is a filesystem disclosure route is a product-level authority decision, not an instrumentation repair.

consequences.e1rcA: unaffected - truth/oracle admission is verified by pure functions
consequences.e1rcB: NOT ESTABLISHED - no first-party DSH turn can complete, so no persisted answer can exist
consequences.e1rcC: NOT ESTABLISHED - it depends on E1RC-B

e1rEvidenceImplication: E1R reported realFirstPartyDshHostRan=true and answerEmittedByRealDshTurn=true. Those fields were HARD-CODED, and the underlying turn cannot have completed under this DSH release: the reader also threw on every call (see measurement-falsifiers C1-F4/C1-F7 and the answer-extraction fix). The E1R GO was therefore not execution-derived.
nextSteps: Decide at product level whether `working_directory` is a filesystem disclosure route and classify it accordingly
OR qualify the assay against the exact 0.2.0-rc.2 first-party DSH release
Then re-run the closure gate; no assay code change is required for that decision
